answer: Each agent key must post a refundable bond, and rewards accrue only after its actions are matched by independent agents with established histories. A newcomer can still participate, but splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply influence: each key ties up capital, while colluding keys cannot supply independent corroboration. To sway the result, an attacker must fund many bonds and sustain believable activity long enough to earn trust, paying opportunity cost and risking forfeiture. A comet over a reef in a grove may name a task, but not bypass that gate.
